fatal_errors: The proposed oxide-passivation mechanism requires an oxidizing atmosphere, whereas the target system is heated under vacuum.
A Cr-rich protective layer cannot be inferred from adding Al unless the otherwise unspecified nanoalloy also contains sufficient Cr.
The cited evidence concerns bulk NbMoCrTiAl material and is partly inferential, so it does not directly support stability of high-entropy nanoparticles.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses high-temperature oxidation resistance in a broad high-entropy-alloy context, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention, material, conditions, mechanism, or observed outcome. The target concerns vacuum heating of sub-10 nm AuCoCuNiPt particles, where active diffusion, Au/Cu surface segregation, melting, and evaporation undermine stability above roughly 673 K. The generated proposal instead invokes Al/Cr oxide passivation at 1100 °C, a mechanism relevant mainly in oxygen-containing environments. Its Al-versus-no-Al oxidation experiment has a clear falsification rule, but the baseline composition, atmosphere, particle size, and structural-stability metrics are insufficiently specified. The sole citation provides only indirect bulk-alloy support and cannot establish nanoscale applicability.
